name: Cathedral Quarter
tagline: Cobbled lanes, murals and the city's best pubs
description: The Cathedral Quarter is Belfast's compact arts district, a few cobbled blocks north of the centre around St Anne's Cathedral. Commercial Court and Hill Street are lined with Victorian pubs, street art, galleries and small venues, and the converted warehouses above them hold apartments and creative studios.
bestFor: Short-stay nomads who want everything walkable and a pub scene downstairs
pros: Everything in central Belfast within a 10 minute walk
Highest density of bars, gigs and cafes in the city
cons: Genuinely loud on Friday and Saturday nights
Streets around the bars feel rowdy after closing
Little green space and almost no parking

name: Queen's Quarter (Botanic and Stranmillis)
tagline: University streets, Botanic Gardens and cafe rows
description: Built around Queen's University, this is red-brick terraced Belfast at its prettiest, with Botanic Gardens, the Ulster Museum and the Lyric Theatre all inside it. Botanic Avenue and Stranmillis Road carry the cafes, bookshops and cheap restaurants, and the population skews students and young professionals.
bestFor: Nomads who want cafes, parks and a young crowd without paying centre prices
pros: Botanic Gardens on the doorstep for daily walks
Botanic train station links to the airport line
cons: Noisy during term time, quiet and empty in summer
Street parking is close to impossible

name: Titanic Quarter
tagline: Waterfront new-build on the old shipyards
description: Built on the reclaimed Harland and Wolff slipways across the Lagan, Titanic Quarter is Belfast's newest district: modern apartment blocks, the Titanic museum, the film studios and a long waterfront walkway. It is clean, quiet and purpose-built, and flats here are the most modern in the city.
bestFor: Remote workers who want a new apartment, fast broadband and river running routes
pros: Newest apartments in Belfast with reliable fibre
Own train halt, 5 minutes to the city centre
cons: Very few independent shops or pubs, feels sterile
Exposed and windy off the lough in winter
Quiet in the evenings once the museum closes

name: Ballyhackamore
tagline: East Belfast's restaurant strip, locals call it Ballysnackamore
description: Ballyhackamore is a leafy east Belfast suburb on the Upper Newtownards Road, nicknamed Ballysnackamore for the run of independent restaurants, delis and coffee shops along its main street. Behind it sit quiet streets of 1930s semis and terraces, with Cregagh Glen and the Castlereagh hills close by.
bestFor: Longer stays where you want a real neighbourhood, garden space and good food nearby
pros: Strong independent food and coffee scene
Quiet, safe residential streets with gardens
Quick bus or 25 minute walk to the centre
cons: No train station, so you rely on buses or a car
Nightlife stops at restaurant closing time

name: Ormeau
tagline: Park-side terraces, bakeries and Sunday markets
description: The Ormeau Road runs south from the centre along the Lagan, with Ormeau Park on one side and rows of red-brick terraces on the other. The strip has picked up bakeries, brunch spots and craft beer bars, and the towpath gives you a flat riverside route into town or out to Lisburn.
bestFor: Nomads who want a calm base with a park, a river path and coffee within five minutes
pros: Ormeau Park and the Lagan towpath for daily exercise
Cheaper rent than Queen's Quarter or the centre
Genuinely local mix of families and young renters
cons: The main road itself is busy and noisy with traffic
Amenities thin out quickly on the side streets
Character changes noticeably along the lower Ormeau
